title: Releases
text:
NoteMostly written by AI



Most of the text on this site, and most of the code behind it, was written by Anthropic’s Claude Code agents working under my direction. The outbreak produces a new situation report every day, and I wanted this data out fast and kept current, which I couldn’t have done by hand. The numbers are computed by the pipeline and checked against the reports (here’s how), but the writing was done in a hurry and will have mistakes. If you find one, please open an issue or get in touch. — Vince Buffalo
Every data release is a git tag named data/<date>-r<n> (six tags from August are plain data/<date>), where the date is that of the newest report the build read. Once I publish a tag I never move it or delete it, so a downstream model pinned to a tag can always get back to the same data. To rebuild a release byte for byte, check out its tag and run make fetch-pinned, then make build streams. In the table, Cut is the day the release was published.

title: Releases
text:
Release notes

data/2026-10-22-r0
daily update
Cut automatically by scripts/daily_update.py: every release gate passed (tests, verdict, export quotes, fresh-clone rebuild).
Fixes merged since the last release (see each pull request for what moved):

data: fetch for 2026-10-24
care: a capitalised lead-in opens a passage, and bullet glyphs set apart from their text are dropped – sitrep 158 ends Ituri’s bullet with no full stop (“dans 4 CTE Au Nord-Kivu”) and puts four displaced glyphs inside it (“431 patients • • • • sont hospitalisés”), so Ituri’s row carried Nord-Kivu’s census of 509, its 332/410 beds and ten recoveries, and Nord-Kivu had no row



data/2026-10-20-r1
daily update
Cut automatically by scripts/daily_update.py: every release gate passed (tests, verdict, export quotes, fresh-clone rebuild).
Fixes merged since the last release (see each pull request for what moved):

onset: stacking order measured per render – 059-062 stack dead under alive, and both readers had folded the deaths into alive (060: 27 dead of 1,792, now 482 of 1,817, equal to epiforecasts on every day)
onset: bar_pitch’s docstring describes the tick regression it does; blog-onset target, and blog figure scripts no longer cut a data revision
onset: read bars through the incomplete-data band rather than at it
onset: read the long-axis renders – the grey y axis is the panel corner, slots clear the border, ticks counted gap by gap; anchor rows for 103-159



data/2026-10-20-r0
daily update
Cut automatically by scripts/daily_update.py: every release gate passed (tests, verdict, export quotes, fresh-clone rebuild).
New data. Sitreps 158, 159, data date 2026-10-18 → 2026-10-20: 152 confirmed cases and 85 deaths nationally in windows from the previous data date.
Not breaking. No code, register or schema changed.


data/2026-10-18-r0
sitreps 128–157, an eighth province, cases outside the DRC, and four corrections to published history
Breaking. A new province, a population denominator that moves, new files, and changed values in rows downstream models have already fitted. What to do is at the end.
New data. Twenty-nine reports, sitreps 128–157 (142 was never published), data date 2026-09-18 → 2026-10-18.

Nord-Ubangi joins at sitrep 155 (2026-10-16), two cases and one death in Wapinda — «qui devient la huitième province touchée». The reports’ own frame widens to 178 health zones in eight provinces, so the national population in meta.json moves 35,581,745 → 37,510,436. New *_nord_ubangi files.
Cases counted outside the DRC. exports_uganda.tsv, exports_kenya.tsv, exports_nigeria.tsv, exports_france.tsv: cumulative totals at the dates a primary source prints them, keeping apart what each source calls imported, imported from the DRC, linked, and of origin still under investigation (Nigeria’s case, which flew in from Uganda). The per-case table, the printed totals and the gap between them are in reference/export_cases.tsv, export_counts.tsv and export_reconciliation.tsv. Every quote is checked against a hashed snapshot of its page (make fetch-exports, make check-exports). uganda_exports.tsv is unchanged; see vsbuffalo/ebola-bdbv-data#1 for why its two pins need replacing.
care_census_dedicated_nord_kivu.tsv. From sitrep 124 Nord-Kivu prints a total and the part of it in dedicated treatment structures, and computes its occupancy on the part. care_census_nord_kivu keeps the total; the new file is the part. Fit one, never both (note).
meta.json gains opening: each province’s first case and death cumulative, which no row of its flow files holds because a flow is the cumulative differenced (note).

Corrections to published values.

Sud-Kivu loses one case it never had. Sitreps 010–011 filed Nord-Kivu’s Kalunguta under Sud-Kivu, and the forward fill kept the case in Sud-Kivu’s stream on every later day — 1 over its printed row on all 131 dates. Two rows in registers/zone_province_overrides.tsv now apply what the front pages state; Nord-Kivu counts that case from 24 May rather than 27 May. A test now requires every province to end at a zero gap against its printed row.
Care splits read from the meal clause. Tshopo (sitreps 125–131) and Haut-Uélé (127–128) published confirmed/suspected care counts that were counts of patients fed («4 confirmés et 2 suspects ont bénéficié d’un repas chaud»). Removed.
A false absconder. Tshopo’s on 2026-09-06 (sitrep 115) was the «1 évadé» in the experimental-treatment cohort’s outcome list, an outbreak-to-date count. Removed, along with the same clause on sitreps 129–132.
checks means what it says. closes now requires an exact check (a split that sums, a printed rate that divides out). 112 rows whose only passing check was a bound such as recoveries ≤ exits are now unchecked: 83 in care_exits_recovered, 19 in care_exits_deaths, 10 in care_census_confirmed. Nord-Kivu’s post-124 care rows no longer read as contradicts. No count changes.

Source defects found and handled, each pinned by a test: the date label renamed from «Date de rapportage» to «Date du rapport» (sitrep 137); sitrep 150’s front page printing 12 October for an 11 October report (registers/printed_date_errata.tsv); the zone table touching the page footer on 154 and 157 and orphaning every province after Ituri; a highlight bullet drawn over the front-page tiles on 143–147; the care prose’s per-province census wording, which had silently emptied the province census for three weeks.
Not advanced. The onset digitiser refuses every chart from sitrep 128, so the reporting delay rests on the 2026-09-18 vintage.
Comparison sources refreshed (they check the data and never feed it): INRB-UMIE’s transcription to db4aee1, the epiforecasts scan to 924c0aa, now both pinned in external.lock. Five new disagreements, none ours (note).
Migration. Re-vendor at this tag. Add the Nord-Ubangi files to any province list, and re-read population (or the frame size) from meta.json. If you fit checks == "closes" rows only, expect fewer recovery and care-death rows. If you fit a Nord-Kivu isolation compartment, choose which census file it observes.


data/2026-09-18-r0
sitreps 114–127, and Sud-Ubangi, a seventh province
Breaking. Sud-Ubangi joins at sitrep 119 (2026-09-10), one case and one death in Bulu, and the reports widen their own frame from 151 zones in six provinces to 167 in seven, so the national population in meta.json moves 31,898,994 → 35,581,745. New *_sud_ubangi files. Fourteen new reports, data date 2026-09-04 → 2026-09-18. scripts/fetch_geography.py now regenerates the geography and population references from a declared list of affected provinces, checked against the zone count the reports print. Two defects in our own readers fixed: the upstream check failed on non-ASCII filenames, and an infodemic bulletin was being classified as a situation report.
Migration. Re-vendor at this tag; add the Sud-Ubangi files; re-read population.


data/2026-09-04-r0
sitreps 109–113, and flow files state their accumulation window in two columns
Breaking for every consumer of a flow stream. A flow file no longer carries time. It carries window_start and window_stop, the half-open interval [window_start, window_stop) its count accumulated over. Stock files (care_census_*, patients_isolated*, cumul_recovered, uganda_exports) are unchanged and keep time. No file carries both forms.
Migration. window_stop sits where time did and is one day later than it: a row that read 2026-07-13 now reads window_start 2026-07-12, window_stop 2026-07-14. Anything that dates an observation — an axis, a join against the report calendar, a comparison against a data date — wants window_stop minus one day, which is exactly the old time value. In this repository scripts/lib/streams.py does that once for every consumer.
No published count changes. 106 flow files, 4,316 rows: every total, every row and every observation is identical to data/2026-08-30-r6. The conversion is window_start = time - (days_covered - 1), window_stop = time + 1, applied at the single write site in build_streams.py, and all 4,210 interior boundaries tile exactly — no gaps, no overlaps.

What the old form could not say
A row’s window was inferred from the gap to the row before it. Delete an interior row and its neighbour silently widened to cover two days: the model still fit and reported a different answer, with nothing in the file saying so. That is why the omit-and-record convention of registers/window_merged_rows.tsv existed, and why correctness lived in a script and a register rather than in the data.
The first row of every file was worse than silent. It has no predecessor, so its window was not recoverable at all and a consumer inferring from row spacing had to assume one day. Twenty-five of the 106 flow files open on a window wider than that — lab_national on seven days, deaths_national on five — and those first rows now say so for the first time. This is the one place the new form changes what a consumer reads, and it is a correction.


The gate that replaces the row-spacing check
accumulation_windows no longer compares days_covered against row spacing. It checks three things on every flow row, all fatal: positive width, window_stop - window_start == days_covered, and window_start equal to the previous row’s window_stop. days_covered survives as provenance — exactly the window’s width, gated to stay so — and remains the right divisor for a daily rate. n_report_days is not, and never was, a denominator.
Overlaps and gaps are both fatal. Every stream published here covers its span without holes: the flow families that go quiet carry an NA row for the silent day rather than skipping it. A gap appearing means a builder dropped a row.


Two corrections riding along
n_report_days was a constant 1 on the daily companion streams, which is right wherever a widened window came from the source skipping a report — one report day still fed the row — and wrong on the three rows widened by window_merged_rows.tsv, where the source did publish on both days. Those rows (cases_daily_ituri, deaths_daily_ituri, deaths_daily_nord_kivu at 2026-07-13) now read 2. Invisible while the window was inferred; visible the moment the row states it.
registers/stream_families.tsv and the repository README both still described the care streams as carrying a row on every report day, and the README stated the grid was “report days, never calendar days”. Both were superseded when the grid became calendar days; a row now exists on every calendar day a flow family spans. The register text is what meta.json and the generated data dictionary publish, so the stale sentence had been shipping to consumers.



data/2026-08-30-r6
three clamped-zero rows deleted, not carried, so the province filter stops collapsing on 12 July
Breaking for a consumer reading cases_daily_ituri, deaths_daily_ituri or deaths_daily_nord_kivu at daily resolution across 12–13 July 2026. Each file loses its 2026-07-12 row; the 2026-07-13 row is unchanged in value and its days_covered becomes 2. No published total moves.

What was there and why it broke a filter
The source’s own province table went mid-redistribution on 12 July: Ituri’s cumulative cases fell by 39 and deaths by 23, Nord-Kivu’s deaths fell by 1, each a downward revision our carry-forward (carry_forward in build_streams.py, recorded row by row in revisions.tsv) clamps to zero and pays off on the next row that moves upward enough to absorb it. All three deficits close in full on 13 July, so the existing published values were already exactly right: 13 July’s 63 Ituri cases is -39 + 102, its 30 deaths -23 + 53, and Nord-Kivu’s 9 deaths -1 + 10.
The clamped zero itself was the problem, independent of being correct. A zero that isn’t a reported observation still gets scored as one: in a particle filter run against these streams at daily resolution, that single row collapsed the effective sample size from 19,200 particles to 2.2, and pinned the latent trajectory across the date by construction.


Why deletion and not NA
An NA row closes an incidence bin at its own time (docs/camdl-data-spec.md in the modelling repo, “Missing observations: NA is a hole, not a zero”). Marking 12 July NA alone would leave 13 July a one-day window still carrying the two-day total of 63 — the same class of defect, the other direction: a count scored against less flow than it represents instead of more. Deleting the row is the encoding the spec itself names for exactly this case: “the following row’s exposure window silently widens to span the gap” is a caution against deleting when the surviving count does not already cover the gap. Here it does, by construction, because the carry paid the deficit into 13 July before either row was written.


What licenses deleting these three rows and not others
registers/window_merged_rows.tsv is new: a hand-authored register, one row per (stream, column, date) deleted, each justified by the arithmetic above. build_streams.py’s merge_windows reads it and re-verifies every entry against the series it just built — the named row must exist, must not be the first or last row of its stream, and its carried value must be exactly zero — before deleting it and recomputing the following row’s days_covered. A register entry that no longer matches (a re-extraction changes the series under it) stops the build rather than silently deleting the wrong row.
This is deliberately not a general rule the build applies to every clamped zero it finds. revisions.tsv carries two more rows of the identical shape — cases_daily_nord_kivu and deaths_daily_nord_kivu, 2026-06-11, discharged in full by 2026-06-13 — left as a published carried zero because extending this treatment to them has not been decided. The Haut-Uélé deficit spanning 18–22 July is a different shape entirely: it discharges over five rows, two of which are genuine reported zeros, and deleting any one of them would leave a negative count for its neighbour to carry — merge_windows refuses this by construction, since a deleted row must be interior with the deficit fully absorbed by the very next row.


What a consumer should do
A daily-resolution reader of the three affected streams sees a two-day gap in the observation schedule at 12–13 July instead of a zero on 12 July, exactly as days_covered = 2 on the 13 July row already stated before this release — that field was correct throughout; only the row set is now consistent with it. A reader at weekly resolution, or of cases_daily_national / deaths_daily_national / deaths_daily_nord_kivu’s national counterpart, is untouched: none of those files had a clamped row here.



data/2026-08-30-r5
r4 does not rebuild; and the rows we said we published were not reachable
Take this instead of r4. Two defects, both ours, both found by a consumer rather than by our gate.

r4 does not rebuild, and our release gate did not catch it
make streams acquired a dependency on make onset — it reads the reporting delay that onset produces — and nothing in the documented build path supplied it. A consumer running make build streams, which is the documented path, stopped at the guard.
Our own gate passed because it ran make onset in between. That is the whole defect: a gate that exercises an order no consumer uses is not a gate. It is fixed by declaring the dependency (streams: onset) rather than by teaching the gate a special order, and release-check now runs exactly make build && make streams — the same two commands a consumer runs.
The guard itself stays. An empty reporting-delay field reads as “no delay” rather than “not measured”, and that distinction is worth a failed build.


The rows we said we published were in a directory nobody copies
burial_alerts.csv and reporting_delay.csv were written to data/build/series/. A consumer takes data/build/streams/. So the burial-alert rows — asked for specifically so the modelling side could pool and weight them itself rather than trust our pooled figure — were announced as delivered and never arrived.
The layering, stated once so this does not recur:

data/build/series/ is internal. Per-report parses carrying statuses, refusal reasons and verbatim quotes, shaped for auditing our extraction against the page. Its shape changes whenever an extractor changes and nothing downstream should pin it.
data/build/streams/ is the interface. Stable names, hash-pinned, documented in the generated dictionary.



streams/reference/, new
Row-level tables a consumer pins and hashes but never fits:
reference/burial_alerts.tsv     82 rows   the death-alert ledger, per province-day
reference/reporting_delay.tsv  165 rows   the delay distribution, per onset cohort
meta["reference"] describes each with its row count and columns.
They are deliberately not streams and not in the stream dictionary. A stream is time-indexed, sits on a declared observation grid, and carries a coverage contract in days_covered and n_report_days. A province-day ledger and a delay distribution have none of that, and listing them as streams would make the dictionary’s promises false for two of its entries.
A test now asserts that meta["swab_coverage"] is exactly the pooling of the published burial_alerts.tsv rows, so the summary can never become a number with no rows behind it.
Consumers must add the two paths explicitly — they sit in a subdirectory, so a top-level glob will not find them.



data/2026-08-30-r4
the onset-to-report delay, because the streams and a model’s confirmation event are not the same instant
Not breaking. One field added to meta, one new series file; no stream file changes and no value moves.

The gap this measures
cases_* is indexed by report date. A model’s projected quantity is a confirmation event. Those are different instants and nothing published so far said how far apart. data/build/series/reporting_delay.csv now carries the distribution, per onset-month cohort, and meta["reporting_delay"] the summary.


Pooling it is the one way to get it badly wrong
onset month      n     mean    median   p90    status
2026-04          3    115.0 d    115    117    still arriving
2026-05         87     79.3 d     77    102    still arriving
2026-06        161     39.1 d     37     67    still arriving
2026-07      1,398     10.2 d      9     19    settled
2026-08      1,002      7.1 d      7     13    still arriving
Pooled over everything the mean is 13.2 days. That figure describes no case in particular and overstates the routine delay by roughly a factor of two. The May and June cohorts were not slow to be reported: the epidemic’s early history was reconstructed retrospectively, months after the fact. The routine delay is the July cohort’s — mean 10.2 d, median 9, p90 19.
So no pooled number is published. usable_cohort names the most recent settled cohort, which is July; a cohort is settled when its follow-up has outrun its own 90th percentile. August’s 7.1 d is right-truncated and biased downward — cases with recent onset and a long delay have not been reported yet.
Picking on settledness alone would have returned June, because the early cohorts are settled precisely by being old. Recency is the second discriminator and both are needed.


The long tail is a bigger problem than the shift
Of the cases appearing in each report month — and all of them land in that month’s cases_* bins regardless of when the person fell ill:
              <=14 d    15-30 d    >30 d    >60 d
July           77.7%      16.1%     6.2%     1.8%
August         77.8%      11.9%    10.3%     4.9%
Roughly a tenth of each month’s reported cases had onset more than a month earlier, and that share is growing. This is the same phenomenon as the 22 July harmonisation, which registers/retrospective_batches.tsv records as two named days — but the triangle shows it is continuous rather than confined to the days the source announces. cases_excluding_backlog removes the declared spikes and does not touch this.


How to use it
Convolve with reporting_delay.csv, do not shift by a mean. The distribution is heavily right-skewed — median 9 against a p90 of 19 in the settled cohort — so a single lag parameter fits the centre and misfits both tails.



data/2026-08-30-r3
the safe-burial pillar’s alert ledger, and the swab constants stop living in prose
Not breaking. One field is added to meta; no stream file changes and no value moves. Re-vendor to pin the swab-coverage figures by tag instead of copying them out of a message.

Why this exists
Swab coverage — what fraction of death alerts end in a body actually swabbed — bounds how much of the true mortality the confirmed-death series can see, since a death never swabbed can never become a confirmed case. A model that declares an ascertainment constant is declaring this quantity.
It has been travelling as digits in prose. Figures were derived by an uncommitted ad-hoc analysis, published, corrected once, and then sat in a consumer’s configs at the pre-correction value for three days. No target regenerated them, so nothing could have caught the drift. That is what this release fixes: the numbers are now a build artefact with a rule behind them.


scripts/extract_burial_alerts.py, new
One row per province per report day in data/build/series/burial_alerts.csv — 82 rows across 5 provinces — carrying the pillar’s own counts along the path a death takes:
alerts raised  ->  bodies the team reached  ->  bodies swabbed
plus burials carried out, failures, the report’s own printed percentage, the verbatim sentence, and how the row was licensed. bodies_reached is almost always empty: the reports print that inner step once in 102.
29 of 82 rows are licensed by the document’s own arithmetic — 14 reproduce a printed percentage, 15 satisfy the identity that bodies swabbed plus failures equals alerts raised. The rest publish as unchecked, which is honest rather than silent. Five sentences were refused.


Two readings the extraction had to get right
The carried-over alert count appears in three constructions, and two of them mean the opposite of the third. reports here is from reporter, to postpone — a body not reached that day:
"72 alertes de décès du jour et 23 reports"     -> 72 + 23 = 95
"93 alertes de décès reçues, dont 13 reports"   -> 93 already
"a reçu 37 alertes (15 reports)"                -> 37 already
The parenthetical reads as though it could be either, and the source settles it. 25 August, Nord-Kivu: «le pilier EDS a reçu 37 alertes (15 reports) : 36 corps swabés, un échec de swab» — 36 swabbed plus 1 failure is 37, the stated total, not 37 + 15. Reading it as an addition inflated five Ituri and Nord-Kivu denominators by 10 to 17 alerts each.
The laboratory section uses the same word for a different thing. «Bas-Uélé : 1 swab reçu et testé» is a specimen arriving at a bench, not a body a burial team reached. Parsed unscoped it becomes a burial row asserting one body swabbed in Bas-Uélé. The extraction is scoped to the pillar’s own section rather than to the word.


meta["swab_coverage"], new
Per province: the value, its numerator and denominator, the province-day count, the sitreps drawn from, and the window.
ituri       0.6585  = 1149/1745  over 21 province-days
nord_kivu   0.9242  =  914/ 989  over 23
haut_uele   0.9024  =   37/  41  over 10
bas_uele    0.5000  =    3/    6  over  2
Published per province and deliberately not pooled. A case-weighted average uses a consumer’s own case counts, which belong on the consumer’s side; what only this repository can do is verify each province against the page.
The denominator is alerts raised, so the figure spans the whole path and carries the alert-to-reached loss inside it. It is not the inner swabbed-over-reached step — the two differ, and on the one day the source decomposes it (sitrep 099: 93 alerts, 76 reached, 60 swabbed) they are 0.645 against 0.789. The field name is the only thing that would tell them apart, so the definition ships beside the number.
Tshopo still has nothing. One row, and it carries no alert count.


What the reproducible figures change
Against the values last published in prose, Ituri and Nord-Kivu move by less than 0.03. Haut-Uélé moves from 0.750 to 0.902 on 10 province-days and 41 alerts — a small-sample number that has now moved twice, which is itself the finding: it should be given a prior, not a point.


One caution that travels with the numbers
Coverage is not a constant. Sitrep 108 records 9 bodies left unswabbed for community resistance in Ituri, and the reports began quantifying refusals only on 30 August. Coverage moves with community acceptance, which is plausibly correlated with transmission itself, so a fixed value — and a maximum especially — is optimistic during a resistance episode. The caution is carried in meta beside the value rather than left in a release note.



data/2026-08-30-r2
population is the source’s frame, and says so in the file
Not breaking. One field changes type, one field is added, no stream file changes. meta["population"] values become integers; their sum is 31,898,994, exactly as in r1. Re-vendor to pick up the declaration; no fit result moves.

What population is a population of, which the file did not previously say
The table was built by iterating the publication list, so publishing three provinces gave a national denominator of 18,334,303 and publishing six gave 31,898,994 — for a population that had not changed by one person. A consumer deriving a susceptible pool from it was being re-scaled by an extraction decision made here. That is the wrong coupling and it is removed: the table is now derived from the geography and is unaffected by which provinces this build publishes.
The frame is the source’s own, and the six-province sum is the right one. Sitrep 108: «60 des 151 (39,7%) zones de santé des six provinces restent affectées depuis le début de l’épidémie en RDC». Six provinces, 151 health zones, and the pinned geojson holds exactly those 151. So population is the denominator the reports’ own affected-zone fraction is a fraction of, and the old 18.3M was our publication list narrowing it, not a different definition.
It is also stable in the way that matters: a seventh province reporting a case does not move it, because it is fixed by geography rather than by case counts. Extending it would mean adding geography, which is a deliberate and visible act.


population_frame, new
So that no consumer has to sum a dictionary and infer what the sum means:
"population_frame": {
  "provinces": 6, "health_zones": 151, "national": 31898994,
  "definition": "The six provinces of the response geography, all 151 health
                 zones, affected or not. ...",
  "source":     "WorldPop raster counts aggregated to health zone; ..."
}
Bind population_frame.national rather than summing population: the sum is correct today only because the keys happen to be the frame, which is the coupling this release removes.


Whole people
The underlying figures are WorldPop raster counts aggregated to health zone, so they come out fractional — bas_uele was 1970167.3391360808. Provinces are now rounded, and national is the sum of the rounded provinces, so the parts add to the whole exactly rather than by a few people. A zone carrying a population but no geography now stops the build; its people would otherwise belong to no province and leave the denominator silently.



data/2026-08-30-r1
no data change; the fetch survives a transient network failure
Not breaking. No value changes and no file is added, removed or renamed. Every stream is byte-identical to data/2026-08-30-r0: nothing that produces one differs between the two tags. Re-vendor only if make data-update aborted for you on r0.
The held-file check makes one HEAD request per report and could fail in two ways that mean opposite things. A response carrying a different Content-Length says the document was revised. No response at all says only that we could not look, which is evidence about the network and none about the bytes. Both incremented the same counter and that counter exits 1, so one transient error out of 99 requests aborted the whole pipeline — which is how a consumer stayed pinned to a superseded release for an hour while the URL in question was serving exactly the bytes we already held.
Unreachability now retries once and is then recorded and named on stderr rather than being fatal, the same licence-or-refuse discipline the extraction uses. A successful HEAD that disagrees on size still stops the fetch, and a name that appears in the unchecked list on consecutive runs is a re-picked URL, which is a revision by another route and does need adjudicating.
This is tagged rather than left on main because a consumer pinning by tag runs the fetch script at that tag, so a fix on main would not reach the run that needs it.


data/2026-08-30-r0
sitreps 107–108, and three provinces that were extracted and never published
Not breaking. Values change and 45 files are added. No file is removed or renamed; no column changes on any existing stream. Re-vendor.
First release under the -r0 convention: the first release of a day now carries an explicit revision number. See “Release tags” above.

Three provinces were missing from the published streams
STREAM_PROVINCES stopped at Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé. Tshopo, Sud-Kivu and Bas-Uélé were extracted in full and published nowhere — the series carried them on 46, 88 and 19 province-days, all current — so a consumer reading only the published streams could not see them, and would reasonably conclude the source was not reporting them.
All six now publish. 83 stream files become 128.
They hold 26 confirmed cases against a national 6,100, and share of the national total is the wrong test for whether a place belongs in the release. Bas-Uélé is nineteen days old, has three of its eleven health zones affected, three deaths on four cases, and the reports say it has no treatment centre meeting standards and no partner supporting case management. Tshopo has 19 cases spread across seven of twenty-three zones — a wide footprint for a small count. Sud-Kivu is published though quiet since 2026-05-29, because a stream that exists and is flat says something a missing stream does not.
It is now a gate. build_streams.py stops if a place carries confirmed cases and is neither published nor recorded with a reason in the new registers/excluded_places.tsv. That register ships empty and should stay that way. make verdict reports provinces reported against provinces published.


What that surfaced
The excluding-backlog family skipped any place with no notified stream. Bas-Uélé and Sud-Kivu have none — the banner printed its 24-hour breakdown only for sitreps 059–083 — so their files were never written. A consumer binding the family across provinces would have found two missing. Moving 004 forward collides it with 005, and moving 005 forward collides it with 006, up the series. So 004 is filed as 18 May, against its printed date. INRB’s independently published national series dates that report 18 May as well — corroboration of the placement from a second reader of the same page, not independent evidence about the count.
The full argument, and the printed date recorded beside the filed one, are in registers/external_sitreps.tsv. The build checks the page against the register on every run: if SitRep 004 ever stops printing 19 mai 2026, the judgement was made about a different document and the build stops.


Two extraction corrections that came with them

SitRep 004’s Ituri label falls between two table rows and is lost. The early layout prints the province as a merged cell spanning its zones; here it centres in the gap between Rwampara and Bunia, so the grid records it on a row with no zone name and no counts, which the extraction drops. Only Nord-Kivu survived, and a carry with one anchor cannot split a two-province table: all 33 cases went to Nord-Kivu. Four entries in registers/zone_province_overrides.tsv state what the page states in prose; the result, Ituri 30 and Nord-Kivu 3, is what the report’s own page-1 province table prints.
? is now recognised as a missing-value marker in the front-page banner, alongside ND and the dashes. SitRep 001 writes ? in the three tiles it had no figure for; without that, its value row was not recognised as a value row at all and the Décès confirmés tile beside them refused. It changes no other report in the archive. The ? is still never read as a number, so 001’s recoveries tile still refuses: a report that says it does not know has not said zero.



Checked against INRB
Seven new zone-day comparisons at 2026-05-18, and all seven agree. Total disagreements across the archive are unchanged at 14. Note that INRB’s own two files date SitRep 002 differently — their national series puts it at 17 May, their zone-level series at 15 May, which is the as-of date printed inside that report’s table rather than its reporting date. We file it under 17 May, the date its front page gives.

new file
Not breaking. Nothing is renamed, removed or revalued: no stream file, no column and no number changes. One file is added. If you have fitted anything on data/2026-08-22, you do not need to refit.

Which streams stop early is now stated, not left to be noticed
A stream that stopped weeks ago looks exactly like a current one unless the reader compares two dates in a table, which is the comparison a consumer skips. The dictionary now carries a section listing every stream with no observation at the data date, and how far behind it is. At this release that is patients_isolated_confirmed.tsv, 20 days behind: INSP stopped printing that front-page tile after sitrep 080 (2 August) and none of the twenty reports since carries it. The stream ends because the source ended it, not because extraction failed. It is derived on every build rather than written down, so it stops being true the day the source resumes.


The streams now ship a data dictionary
Until now a consumer holding data/build/streams/ could not answer what is community_deaths_daily_ituri, and what dates does it cover? without reading build_streams.py. meta.json carries only global fields, and its reconciliation block — which does hold first_date / last_date for the streams built by differencing a cumulative — carries no dates at all for the eight community_deaths_* or the five lab_* files, so it could not have answered the second half of that question for thirteen of the thirty-four published files.
data/build/streams/README.md      one row per published file: what it
                                  measures, its resolution, its place, how
                                  many observations, first and last `time`
Every span in it is read back off the file it describes, not out of meta.json. It is generated by the run that writes the streams, so it travels with the vendored data and describes that vintage. It also states, once, the conventions a consumer needs: that a weekly row is scored over its 7-day bin and a daily row covers (previous report day, this report day], that days with no report are absent rather than zero, that no published count is negative, and which columns are observations and which (days_covered, n_report_days, flags, n_provinces) describe the row.
The one thing no build can generate — the sentence saying what a quantity measures — is hand-written in the new register registers/stream_families.tsv, keyed on the observation family rather than on the file, so the four province variants of one quantity cannot come to be described in four different ways. A stream this pipeline writes whose family has no sentence there now stops the build and names the file: a new stream cannot ship undocumented.


Three laboratory files were outside the non-negativity gate
lab_daily_ituri.tsv, lab_daily_nord_kivu.tsv and lab_daily_haut_uele.tsv were written directly rather than through the build’s write_stream, so they never entered the list the build reads back to assert that no published count is negative. They now do. Nothing was wrong with the three files — the gate finds nothing in them at this release — but the assertion the other thirty-one carry had a hole in it exactly where a new stream is most likely to be added.
Consumers need do nothing. The three files are unchanged.

A stream never publishes a negative count again
The source revises downward. When it does, differencing its cumulative gives a negative increment, and a negative was being published into streams whose whole purpose is to be read by an observation model that cannot represent one. Both the weekly and the daily companions now carry the deficit forward: the day of the revision emits 0, and the shortfall is held against subsequent days until it is discharged.
Nothing is silently smoothed. Every carried day is recorded in a new file:
data/build/streams/revisions.tsv     stream, column, time, raw, emitted,
                                     carry_after, flags
raw is what the source published, emitted is what the stream carries, and carry_after is the deficit still outstanding. It is generated by the same run that writes the streams and is never hand-maintained. Twenty-two rows at this release, eight of them where raw is negative, all between 11 June and 22 July. Two build assertions now fail the build if any stream carries a negative or if a carry is left undischarged at the end of a series.
Consumers who need the unadjusted series should read revisions.tsv alongside the stream and add raw - emitted back.

Nothing downstream would have said so: every check the pipeline has asks whether the reports we hold reconcile, and a day never fetched reconciles by being absent. The ascertainment figure would have drawn 19 August as a day INSP published nothing.
fetch_sitrep_index.py now probes the numbers its listing skips, at the bare-numbered URL and in the directory the reports either side were uploaded to. A hit is reported as unresolved for someone to read the front page, not guessed at.
Five earlier report-days remain absent — 29 (12 Jun), 43 (26 Jun), 45 (28 Jun), 75 and 76 (28–29 Jul). Each is a real missing day rather than a skipped number: the reports either side step two or three days. They are not in the media listing under any name and not at the bare-numbered URL, so they need a different channel.


Bas-Uélé was published as 11 cases against a printed 2
Three extraction defects, all in the geometry layer, all from the coloured band the province rows have been printed on since sitrep 094. Word draws that band as one filled rectangle per cell per printed line, and every filled rectangle was being read as a cell whose four sides are rules.
The one that matters most for a consumer produced a wrong number rather than a missing row. Bas-Uélé’s two health zones are divided by no horizontal rule; the rows fused, and because a space is this source’s thousands separator the fused 1 1 parsed as eleven. Sitreps 099 and 100 both published Bas-Uélé as 11 cases and 10 deaths. It is 2 and 1.
The other two: on a row whose label wraps (Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé are the only names long enough) the shading cut the row in half, Nord- kept the counts, matched no province, and both provinces were filed as health zones — sitrep 098 failed its national identity by exactly their 845 cases. And on sitrep 099 the same paint welded the table to the page-footer bar, so page 3 chained to nothing and the report yielded 25 rows and no national total.
All four new reports now reconcile with residual 0.


What moved
Four new observation days, 19–22 August, each days_covered = 1. The daily national series runs contiguously to 22 August. Ituri’s 098–100 values are corrected — its cumulative had been read as spiking to 6,200 and falling back, and the carry-forward that absorbs a downward revision published the spike. Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé totals are unchanged, because their 098 values were missing rather than wrong, and a gap does not move a total that is final − initial.
A note on report 100, uncorrected. It states 55 new confirmed cases twice, and its zone table’s national row prints 55, but its cumulative moves +56. Localised, the whole gap is one case in Haut-Uélé, whose own daily figure is one short of its own cumulative movement. The streams difference the cumulative and carry 56; the printed 55 is retained as new_cases in zone_table.csv. No gate currently compares a printed daily flow against a cumulative movement.
